## Second instance, in a **different package** — and it dequeued a second unrelated PR

`domain:engine` dispatching seat, 2026-09-07T05:5xZ. ⛔ Still an observation, no grading, no `domain:*`, no priority — this is added because it widens the card's population, not because it changes its verdict.

### The new instance

Queue CI run [34086147182](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34086147182), `Test Core (4/6)` — **17 jobs, exactly one failing test**:

```
FAIL  packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.queue-delivery.test.ts:279
  > EmailService — queue delivery on
  > still refuses the queue for attachments OVER the limit, and stores nothing (#5177)
    ↳ Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
```

It dequeued **#16442**, whose eight changed files include **zero** under `packages/plugins/plugin-email/`, and whose own PR CI is 41/41 with 0 failing on the same head.

### The same probe, the same answer, a different package

| probe | `driver-sql` (this card, 05:4xZ) | `plugin-email` (new) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `testTimeout` in the package's `vitest.config.ts` | **absent** | **absent** |
| explicit per-test timeouts in the failing file | **0** | **0** |
| effective budget | vitest default **5000 ms** | vitest default **5000 ms** |
| what it cost | dequeued #16430 (a changeset-body-only PR) | dequeued #16442 (a `@objectstack/core` narrowing) |

The control table from the original filing is unchanged and still fires: six packages in this repo **do** set `testTimeout` — `driver-mongodb` 30_000, `service-datasource` 60_000, `spec` 60_000, `qa/http-conformance` 30_000, `plugin-auth` 10_000, `metadata-fs` 10_000.

### ⚠️ What this does and does not change about the card

**Does**: the population is wider than "the one live-DB driver". Two packages, two queue-only timeouts, two dequeued PRs, in one night — and neither failing test belongs to the PR it dequeued. Whatever the fix is, scoping it to `driver-sql` alone would leave the second instance standing.

**Does not**: it does not make the two instances the *same* defect. `driver-sql`'s is specific and derivable — 24 live round-trips to two real servers inside a 5 s budget. `plugin-email`'s failing test is in-process and has no live server, so **why** it needs more than 5 s is a separate question this seat has not answered, and ⛔ raising its budget without answering it would convert a visible flake into a slow test nobody notices. That question belongs to whoever takes this card.

⚠️ ⛔ **And the direction NOT to take by reflex**: a repo-wide default is the tempting fix and it is the one that costs the most — it raises the ceiling for every fast in-process suite, which is where a 5 s guard is doing real work. The two derivations (what a live-server matrix needs; whether an in-process email test should need it at all) are separate, and the second one may end in "fix the test" rather than "raise the budget".

Triage: lands in `domain:engine` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql`); rationale: class (a) — ⭐ **this one did not predict a cost, it measured one that was already paid.** PR #16430 (`+46 / −1` on a single `.changeset/*.md`, **zero** files under `driver-sql/`) was dequeued at `00:45:57Z` with `CI_FAILURE` on a test its diff cannot reach, and the queue rebuilt everything behind it. `Bug`.

`priority:p2`. Two facts set it there and both are on the card: the failure mode is a **merge-queue dequeue**, which is strictly more expensive than a red PR check, and the 24h ledger recorded **0** other queue failures — so this is the first instance, which is exactly when the budget question is cheap to answer rather than tangled with a backlog of re-runs.

⭐ **The firing control is what makes this gradeable rather than arguable**, and it should survive into the PR: six packages set `testTimeout`; `driver-mongodb` — the *other* live-DB driver — sets **30_000**; `driver-sql`, the one package whose suite talks to **two** live servers, sets **none** and inherits vitest's 5000ms. A complete grep, a named comparator, and an explicit statement of what the finding does *not* claim (5s is fine for the in-memory / SQLite cells, which are the majority). That last fence is the difference between a budget card and a "raise the timeout" reflex.

⭐ **This is a missing budget, not a flaky assertion, and the card proves it rather than asserting it**: §2 deliberately does no sleeping — the file's own head docblock records that #11572 kept *"§1, §1b and §2 … with no sleep between them"* because the unslept same-millisecond path **is** §2's subject. What it spends is network: `ROUNDS = 6` × four live round-trips = **24 live round-trips in one test**, with the cursor comparison deliberately made server-side so it happens in the column's own type. ⇒ ⛔ Do not "fix" §2 by sleeping, backdating or driving its clock. The two prior repairs to this file (#11572 drove §3 instead of racing it; #13691 moved §3's validity ceiling) touch §3 only and ⛔ must not be extended to §2 — doing so would delete the thing the test measures.

⛔ **Do not treat the next occurrence as a flake and re-run it.** A re-run was the right response to *this* instance and it was already spent (#16430 re-queued at `00:49:01Z`). The card is about the class, and the cause is named.

Route — the two questions the card says a dev must settle rather than assume, ratified here as blocking, not optional:

1. **One budget or two.** A package-wide `testTimeout` also raises the ceiling for the fast in-memory cells, weakening them as a guard; a live-cells-only budget keeps them strict at the cost of being carried explicitly. ⇒ Decide and say which, in the PR.
2. **What number, derived from what.** ⛔ **Not copied from `driver-mongodb` by analogy** — 30_000 is that package's number, not a repo constant. Derive it from the observed live round-trip cost, the discipline #13691 applied to §3's span ceiling: a bound derived from the conclusion it guards, not picked. An undated, underived timeout is indistinguishable from one raised to silence a real regression.

Sibling note: **#16497** (core's discriminator pin, same default 5000ms) is graded `p3` today — same class, but observed only on a shared dev box and never on CI. This card outranks it because the cost here is on the record.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.
